headline: Attacks on shipping around the Strait of Hormuz pushed Brent above 117 dollars and WTI up 3.99 percent to 103.44, and the oil driven inflation scare left gold within about 1.3 percent of its 52 week low and the Dow down 652 points, three days before the Fed decision on 28 October.

summary.us: The Dow fell 652.82 points or 1.23 percent on Friday to 52,215.16 while the S&P 500 slipped 0.52 percent to 7,623.68 and the Nasdaq Composite eased 0.21 percent to 25,955.34, with crude above 100 dollars and caution before the 28 October Fed decision driving the move. The S&P 500 and Nasdaq both booked a second straight weekly loss after Thursday's 2.6 percent Nasdaq slide, which followed a Lam Research warning on chip supply constraints into 2027 and fresh questions about how the AI data centre buildout is financed, with CoreWeave 2032 bonds quoted near 78 cents on the dollar.
summary.india: The Sensex and Nifty closed lower on Friday as Brent above 113 dollars hit oil importers, with Hindalco, Adani Enterprises and Tata Steel the heaviest Nifty drags and Bank Nifty down 1.16 percent to 54,287. IT was the exception, with Infosys up 3.21 percent and TCS up 2.56 percent on hopes that the overnight rout in AI linked stocks sends work back to traditional services firms, while FIIs bought about 888 crore rupees and DIIs about 3,235 crore rupees of cash equities and the rupee closed 12 paise weaker at 94.93.
summary.global: Tokyo's Nikkei 225 ended Friday 0.34 percent lower at 62,693.16 on the crude move and a rotation out of technology, while the Hang Seng rose 0.69 percent to 23,093.37 as Chinese EV makers steadied. Europe had already dropped on Thursday, with the DAX off 1.07 percent and the Euro Stoxx 50 down 1.94 percent, and on Friday the US 10 year yield closed near 4.99 percent while the dollar index held just above 101.75 and copper gained 2.12 percent on COMEX.

weekly.narrative: Two forces ran the week and both pointed at the cost of capital. Attacks on shipping around the Strait of Hormuz, including Iranian claims that seven vessels were hit or mined, took Brent above 117 dollars and WTI past 100, and because that lands as an inflation shock rather than a growth scare it lifted rate expectations instead of safe havens: gold fell more than 3.5 percent on the week to within about 1.3 percent of its 52 week low and silver hit a year to date low, while the US 10 year held near 4.99 percent. The second force was the AI financing question, which moved from equity multiples to credit, with a Lam Research warning on chip supply into 2027 knocking the Nasdaq 2.6 percent on Thursday, CoreWeave 2032 bonds quoted near 78 cents on the dollar, and Jensen Huang arguing the sector is short of capital rather than demand. India inverted the pattern, with the Nifty pressured by the oil bill and foreign selling while IT rallied on a reverse AI trade that reads weaker AI capex as work returning to traditional services firms, and the rupee closed at 94.93 against the dollar. Next week stacks the catalysts: the Fed decision on 28 October with a hike priced near 7.6 percent, Microsoft and Alphabet that same evening, Amazon plus Q3 GDP and September PCE on 29 October, the Bank of Japan on 30 October, and in Mumbai the listing of the 30,213 crore rupee Jio Platforms issue alongside five new mainboard IPOs.
